accumulated_total_gas_count.class: name drops a qualifier the source states

flags.quote: Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of all gas species delivered by injection after plasma breakdown, summed across species.
flags.rule: I1.10_qualifier_preservation: the record states the counting basis is equivalent-electron inventory (N_eq = sum_s z_s N_s), a kind-of-quantity qualifier that separates it from a plain particle count; the incumbent name 'accumulated_total_gas_count' omits 'equivalent_electron', denoting a broader/different quantity, as the nearest neighbours' separations confirm.

I2.7_wrong_physics_qualifier — the name's qualifier 'gas' occupies the qualifier slot where the quantity's defining qualifier is 'equivalent_electron'; every nearest neighbour carrying the same kind of quantity (accumulated_total_gas_equivalent_electron_count, accumulated_total_prefill_gas_equivalent_electron_count, accumulated_argon_equivalent_electron_count_due_to_gas_injection, etc.) states 'equivalent_electron', and the definition specifies a weighted equivalent-electron inventory, not a bare gas count. The name as written denotes a different quantity (a plain particle count) than the source describes.

accumulated_total_prefill_gas_count.class: name drops a qualifier the source states

flags.rule: I1.10_qualifier_preservation: the definition and documentation state the quantity is an equivalent-electron inventory/count ('Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory', 'expressed as an equivalent-electron count'), and the nearest neighbour accumulated_total_prefill_gas_equivalent_electron_count carries the equivalent_electron qualifier that this name lacks; the counting basis (equivalent electrons versus particles/atoms) is identity, not normalisation, so its omission makes the name denote a broader quantity (a raw particle count) rather than the equivalent-electron count the record defines.

accumulated_tritium_prefill_count.class: name drops a qualifier the source states

flags.rule: I1.10_qualifier_preservation — the record states the counting basis 'equivalent electron' (one equivalent electron per tritium atom; equivalent-electron count), a load-bearing qualifier that separates this quantity from a plain tritium atom count, and the incumbent name omits it, denoting a broader/different quantity; neighbours carry 'equivalent_electron' for the same kind of quantity.

repaired_record.description: Tritium prefill count is the amount of tritium introduced by gas injection before plasma breakdown, expressed as one equivalent electron per tritium atom.
repaired_record.documentation:
Tritium prefill count is the accumulated amount of neutral tritium introduced by gas injection during prefill before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each tritium atom contributes one equivalent electron; a neutral diatomic tritium molecule contributes two.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{T,prefill}} = N_{\mathrm{T,prefill}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{T}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{T,prefill}}$ is the tritium equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{T,prefill}}$ is the accumulated count of injected tritium atoms including molecular constituents, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{T}}$ is their introduction rate, $t$ is time, $t_0$ is the prefill start time, and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time.

This quantity counts injected tritium, not the retained or ionized tritium inventory. It excludes post-breakdown gas injection, wall recycling, neutral-beam fueling, and pellet fueling. The equivalent-electron convention is an accounting normalization based on neutral atomic composition, not an actual free-electron count.

It is the tritium contribution to the [total prefill gas count](name:accumulated_total_prefill_gas_equivalent_electron_count), which sums over all injected species. The [accumulated tritium count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_tritium_count_due_to_gas_injection) instead counts tritium introduced after plasma breakdown.
repaired_record.name: accumulated_tritium_prefill_equivalent_electron_count_due_to_gas_injection

The nearest neighbours plasma_decay_time_due_to_disruption and runaway_electron_decay_time_due_to_disruption show the required qualifier this name lacks, so one name cannot denote exactly one quantity.

normalized_collisionality.class: name drops a qualifier the source states

flags.rule: I1.10_qualifier_preservation: the source states the quantity is between two species (interspecies), and the definition confirms it is the ratio of an interspecies collision frequency nu_ab to a characteristic frequency; the incumbent name 'normalized_collisionality' omits the species-pair qualifier, so it denotes a broader quantity (any collisionality) rather than the interspecies one. The nearest neighbours normalized_electron_collisionality and electron_collisionality_normalized_at_pedestal_top carry the species qualifier 'electron', showing this name must separate itself by the species qualifier it lacks.

name-states-its-subject: the name states a normalized collisionality but names no species or population whose collisionality it is; the source identifies a specific subject ('between two species') and the family neighbours (normalized_electron_collisionality, electron_collisionality_normalized_at_pedestal_top) carry the 'electron' subject qualifier that this name lacks, so a reader cannot tell which object's collisionality is meant.

repaired_record.description: Dimensionless ratio of a specified interspecies collision frequency to the characteristic streaming, transit, or bounce frequency used for the plasma population.
repaired_record.documentation:
This collisionality measures the strength of interspecies collisional relaxation relative to collisionless motion along magnetic-field trajectories.

$$
\nu_{ab}^{*} = \frac{\nu_{ab}}{\omega_{\mathrm{char}}}
$$

where $\nu_{ab}$ is the collision frequency between species $a$ and $b$, and $\omega_{\mathrm{char}}$ is the relevant characteristic streaming, transit, or bounce angular frequency; both quantities have reciprocal-time units.

The denominator must be interpreted according to the selected orbit or motion class, so this quantity is distinct from the collision frequency itself. It generalizes the population-specific electron collisionality and complements collisionality at the pedestal top when the characteristic frequency is evaluated there.
repaired_record.name: normalized_interspecies_collisionality

spectral_rate_of_spectrometer_channel.class: name drops a qualifier the source states

flags.quote: number of photoelectrons detected by unit time by a wavelength pixel of the channel
flags.rule: I1.10_qualifier_preservation — the source states the counting basis 'photoelectrons' (detected photoelectrons), and the definition likewise specifies 'photoelectron rate' (dN_pe/dt). The incumbent name 'spectral_rate_of_spectrometer_channel' states only 'rate' with no counting basis, so it denotes a broader quantity (any rate of any counted entity) and drops the stated 'photoelectron' qualifier that separates it from, e.g., photon count or particle rates.

repaired_record.description: Detected photoelectron rate assigned to each wavelength pixel of a spectrometer channel after electronic gain compensation and relative calibration, but before absolute radiometric calibration.
repaired_record.documentation:
This quantity is the spectrally resolved detection rate of photoelectrons produced by a spectrometer channel. It represents the channel response at an individual wavelength pixel rather than an absolutely calibrated optical emission quantity.

The rate for wavelength pixel $p$ is defined by

$$
R_p = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{pe},p}}{dt}
$$

where $R_p$ is the detected photoelectron rate for pixel $p$, $N_{\mathrm{pe},p}$ is the detected photoelectron count assigned to that pixel, and $t$ is time.

The quantity applies separately to each wavelength pixel of the spectrometer channel, with electronic gain compensation and relative channel calibration applied. It is not summed over the spectral range, and it is not an absolute radiance or photon-flux measurement.

Summing the rates over pixels that contain an identified spectral feature produces the corresponding line-integrated signal, represented by [intensity at spectral line](name:intensity_at_spectral_line). The electrical output [voltage of spectrometer channel](name:voltage_of_spectrometer_channel) is a distinct signal quantity and is not this photoelectron rate.
repaired_record.name: spectral_photoelectron_rate_of_spectrometer_channel

I2.7_wrong_physics_qualifier: the qualifier 'surface' asserts a material surface (thermodynamic temperature of an exposed material boundary), but the source bound to this name is an apparent temperature from a processed infrared image — a radiative brightness temperature of the plasma as recorded by a camera channel, not the thermodynamic temperature of a material surface. The qualifier names a different physical quantity than the source describes.

thickness_of_breeder_blanket_layer.class: name drops a qualifier the source states

flags.quote: Thickness of this layer evaluated at the midplane
flags.rule: I1.10_qualifier_preservation — the bound source states the qualifier 'at the midplane' (midplane evaluation locus), but the incumbent name 'thickness_of_breeder_blanket_layer' omits it, so the name denotes a broader quantity (thickness of the layer anywhere) rather than the midplane-evaluated thickness; the target path 'midplane_thickness' confirms the midplane qualifier is load-bearing identity.

I2.7_wrong_physics_qualifier — the source defines the thickness evaluated at the midplane, a midplane qualifier is required to separate this quantity from the general layer thickness; the incumbent name lacks the midplane qualifier and so denotes a different quantity (general through-thickness) than the source's midplane-evaluated thickness.

repaired_record.description: Non-negative geometric separation between the inner and outer material interfaces of a breeder blanket layer along the specified thickness direction.
repaired_record.documentation:
Non-negative geometric separation between the inner and outer material interfaces of a breeder blanket layer is the local through-thickness of that layer along the specified thickness direction. The quantity applies to a single material or functional layer within the blanket, not to the total breeder blanket module build.

The layer thickness is defined by the separation of the two bounding interfaces along the thickness coordinate:

$$
d_\ell = \left|s_{\ell,\mathrm{out}} - s_{\ell,\mathrm{in}}\right|
$$

where $d_\ell$ is the layer thickness in m, and $s_{\ell,\mathrm{in}}$ and $s_{\ell,\mathrm{out}}$ are the signed coordinates in m of the inner and outer layer interfaces along the specified thickness direction.

It is not the toroidal width, poloidal height, surface extent, or volume-equivalent thickness of the layer. It is distinct from module-level quantities such as thickness_of_breeder_blanket_module, [lower_thickness_of_breeder_blanket_module](name:lower_thickness_of_breeder_blanket_module), and [upper_thickness_of_breeder_blanket_module](name:upper_thickness_of_breeder_blanket_module). For a radially stacked layer, the thickness direction is the cylindrical $\hat{R}$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.
repaired_record.name: midplane_thickness_of_breeder_blanket_layer

row_records.statement: One row per (phase, member, pass) for every call this node made, with the flag, the words of the source or the rule that caused it, the reason, and for a repair the decision and proposed name. The full log with prompt digests and token counts is in the run directory.
